column1: # Where each woven Italian plural in lex-it.tsv was read.
# A noun row weaves its second form under an English plural, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. On 2026-10-08 every woven
# Italian plural was read in the headword line of English Wiktionary's
# Italian entry for its noun, rendered as a reader sees it, because the raw
# template mostly leaves the plural to Wiktionary's module: {{it-noun|f}}
# prints "bocca f (plural bocche)". All 173 are among the plurals their own
# noun's line prints, and none was changed: the five whose plural is
# feminine, uova beside uovo, had already stopped being woven, by the rule
# quote is the clause of that line which prints the plural, its qualifiers
# kept, or "invariable" where the line says the plural is the singular. A
# page holds every word of one spelling, so the clause is this word's own
# noun's, of the seed's gender and sense. Two pages hold a second noun of
# this spelling with no such plural: miele, honey, is "plural mieli" where
# miele, the colour, is invariable, and barca, boat, is "plural barche"
# where barca, a sheaf, is uncountable. A noun with a feminine counterpart
# prints its own as "masculine plural", signore beside signora.
# tests/tools/plurals.test.ts requires every noun lex-it.tsv weaves in a
# second form to have a line here with that form, citing the noun's own
# entry, its quote printing the form, and fails on a line outliving its row.
